PRODUCT:
Build a usable Claims Research Lab with five sidebar destinations:
UC01 Salvage valuation; UC02 Damage estimate verification; UC03 Rental extension research; UC04 Loss verification; UC05 War room research with MCP.
Use a restrained professional engineering dashboard: off-white/slate surfaces, dark navy sidebar, teal interaction accents, clear typography, compact readable data tables, status chips, and IBM Plex Mono for trace/code details. Responsive layout. Show the exact project title in the app's About/overview and a shorter navigation label where necessary. No insurer branding or real claim data.

Every screen needs editable scenario inputs, explicit Fixture / Live / Replay mode, a working Run research interaction, progress, findings, an evidence drawer, source coverage/gaps, redacted trace, local review dispositions, run history and JSON/readable exports. Implement the supplied fixture scenarios and arithmetic exactly, with conspicuous Simulated labels. Fixture mode makes no provider calls. Replay must only represent genuine previously recorded live research. Never silently change modes or substitute a fixture for a live error.

SERVER AND LIVE RESEARCH:
PARALLEL_API_KEY is assumed to be supplied as a server environment secret. The actual value is not part of this handoff. Never ask for it in a normal browser input, embed it in client code, use a VITE_ variable, log it, or create a dummy key. If absent, Live shows a clear server-configuration error; finish the rest of the application without blocking on key entry.
Port the HTTP request templates to backend-only handlers. Search/Extract use /v1/search and /v1/extract with x-api-key; Task uses /v1/tasks/runs with the actual output schema object and persisted run IDs. Poll/resume existing runs rather than recreating them. Use the stored provider Basis and exact source excerpts. Calculations use decimal-safe arithmetic and fact references. Keep asking prices, final sales, bids, posted rates and supplier-confirmed quotes distinct. Unknown evidence stays null.
Use the backend's authenticated ownership model for stored runs; do not expose any endpoint that lets unauthenticated visitors spend the API key's credits. A fixture-only public preview is acceptable while live research stays behind authenticated backend access. Include a redacted server configuration status. Follow the run caps, timeout and error requirements in the package.

UC05 MCP:
Implement actual MCP tool discovery/calls to Parallel MCP from the backend when supported. Port the proposed stdio mock-enterprise server to a backend HTTP MCP service if needed; document this transport adaptation. The mock enterprise context stays internal, and only question/public_vehicle/region go out. The canary must not appear in outbound requests. If the platform cannot execute part of the MCP transport, show that part explicitly as not connected; never fabricate a live MCP trace or relabel a direct API call as MCP. Keep the fully working simulated walkthrough available as its own explicit mode.

IMPORTANT CASE SEMANTICS:
- Salvage: pre-loss market evidence is separate from damaged salvage recovery; no unsupported settlement value.
- Damage: exact part condition/fitment and all required cost components before a comparable total; missing labor data stays unresolved.
- Rental: exact dates/branch/class, all required fees and confirmation basis; no fabricated availability or automatic booking.
- Loss: observations vs warnings/forecasts and precise vs ZIP-only matching; no inferred coverage/fraud/claim clearance.
- War room: facts vs hypotheses, sources, contradictions, and real connection status.

VALIDATION AND FINISH:
Run available build/type checks and meaningful tests for the fixture calculations, mode separation, schema mapping, null handling and secret redaction. Inspect the rendered UI in the preview. Keep this as an editor/preview project; do not publish to public production hosting.
